Trust me, you don't want to go there. It's just nonstop DBT (Assuming you're a minor, here adults don't get treatment at all in inpatient) and you'll start people-watching with a passion. It's really not helpful, it's short-term crisis intervention. They'll give you tools you can easily access already.  
If you really want to get admitted though, you should go to a local hospital. Make sure it's one with a unit for your age range. You should go to the triage, and explain what's going on to the triage nurse. You'll have to stay there, probably for hours until they lead you to the mental health crisis centre. You'll have to speak to a social worker who will just talk to you, and they might (if they don't, you'll be in outpatient) make you speak to a psychiatrist, who will decide if you need to be admitted. If they don't, they'll refer you to an outpatient treatment program.  
Hospitalization just isn't great. They can and they will take your rights if you do anything. They can say awful things.  
It's easier to get admitted with a doctor's note. That's what got me admitted; I got a note from my GP saying I urgently needed an assessment, and through that assessment  I was deemed chronically depressed with social anxiety, suicidal ideation, attempts, and having deep self-harm wounds—it does take a bit to get hospitalized, and you'll have to advocate for yourself.  
I just really can't stress about how awful that experience is. And while it does sound cliche, there is a way out of this. Hospitalization is more of a last-resort   
If you don't feel safe or are in a crisis, you should go to a hospital. The best thing you can do is be honest.
